data.text:
Almost five years ago today, we had raised at the earliest opportunity the fundamental objections to the dolomite beach project.

Yet the previous government still built it at the cost of at least P389-M.

And here we are today, with a beach that contributes to flooding due to the closure of three major outfalls as a result of the overall design and construction of the dolomite beach itself.

People can conjecture the motives of this inquiry all they want but this is not about the former President: he has far more serious problems than this dolomite beach controversy.

This is simply about the accountability of environment officials who originated, planned and spent public funds for a clearly non-environmental objective.

The mandate of the Supreme Court is to improve the water quality of Manila Bay. The dolomite beach does nothing to improve the water quality of Manila Bay.

Kahit lumuha pa kayo ng dugo, tuloy ang imbestigasyon sa dolomite beach project.

#WalangPasok: The Valenzuela City government has announced the suspension of online and in-person classes from Kindergarten to Senior High School in both public and private schools on Tuesday, July 22, due to heavy rains and flooding brought by the Habagat.

Classes at Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Valenzuela (PLV) and Valenzuela City Technological College (ValTech) are also suspended.

Meanwhile, for other universities and colleges, the decision on class suspension will be left to the discretion of their respective school administrations. | via Hannah Nicol
